items.title: SQL injection in a login lookup
items.task: get_user builds its SQL by joining the username into the string. Change it so the username is passed to the database as a parameter.

checks.label: The query uses a ? placeholder
The username is passed as a parameter tuple
The username is not joined or formatted into the SQL

hints: The database driver can take the values separately from the SQL text.
In sqlite3, put ? where the value goes and pass a tuple as the second argument of execute().
execute(query, (username,)) - note the comma that makes it a tuple.

items.title: Missing ownership check
items.task: Any logged-in user can read any account by changing the id in the URL. Return the account only if it belongs to the current user; otherwise respond with 404.

checks.label: The owner is compared with the current user
A non-owner gets an error (abort 403 or 404)

hints: The account has an owner_id; the logged-in user has an id.
Compare them before returning anything.
If they differ, abort(404) so the response does not even confirm the account exists.

items.title: Server-side request forgery in a link preview
items.task: fetch_preview downloads any URL it is given, including internal addresses. Restrict it: allow only http/https, check the destination host against an allow-list or refuse private addresses, and do not follow redirects.
items.code:
import requests

def fetch_preview(url):
    resp = requests.get(url, timeout=5)
    return resp.text[:500]

checks.label: The URL is parsed
The scheme is checked
The host is checked against an allow-list or private ranges
Redirects are not followed

hints: Parse the URL first with urllib.parse.urlparse.
Refuse anything that is not http or https, and compare parsed.hostname with a set of allowed hosts.
Pass allow_redirects=False so an allowed host cannot bounce you to an internal one.

items.title: Hard-coded cloud secret
items.task: The secret access key is written in the source file. Read it from the environment instead and remove the literal. (The key shown is the example value from AWS documentation, not a real credential.)

checks.label: The value is read from the environment
No long secret literal remains in the code

hints: import os, then read the value at runtime.
os.environ["AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY"] fails loudly when the variable is missing, which is what you want.
Remember that a key that was committed once must also be rotated.
items.solution:
import os
import boto3

client = boto3.client("s3", aws_secret_access_key=os.environ["AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY"])

items.title: MD5 password hashing
items.task: Passwords are hashed with MD5, which is fast and broken. Switch to a slow, salted password hash (argon2, bcrypt or scrypt).

checks.label: MD5 and SHA-1 are not used
A password hashing function is used (argon2, bcrypt, scrypt or pbkdf2)
The stored hash is verified with the library, not with ==

hints: Use a library made for passwords, such as argon2-cffi or bcrypt.
PasswordHasher().hash(password) creates a salted hash; PasswordHasher().verify(stored, password) checks it.
verify raises an exception on mismatch, so wrap it in try/except and return False.

items.title: Cross-site scripting in a comment box
items.task: showComment inserts the comment as HTML. Insert it as text instead.

checks.label: The text is inserted as text (textContent, innerText or createTextNode)
innerHTML is not assigned

hints: The browser treats innerHTML as markup, so <script> or onerror= in the comment would run.

Create the

with document.createElement and set its textContent.
container.appendChild(p) adds it to the page.

items.title: Path traversal in a file download
items.task: readUpload joins a user-supplied name onto the uploads folder, so ../../etc/passwd escapes it. Resolve the final path and refuse anything outside the uploads folder.

checks.label: The final path is resolved
The result must start with the uploads folder
An escape is rejected (throw, return null or an error status)

hints: path.resolve(BASE, name) turns ../ segments into a real absolute path.
Compare the result with BASE using startsWith(BASE + path.sep).
If it does not start with BASE, throw an error before reading the file.

items.title: Unverified and weakly signed tokens
items.task: verifyToken only decodes the token, so anyone can forge one, and signToken uses a guessable secret. Verify the signature with a fixed algorithm, read the secret from the environment, and give tokens an expiry.

checks.label: The signature is verified (jwt.verify)
The accepted algorithms are fixed
The token is not just decoded
The secret is not a literal like 'secret'
The secret comes from the environment
Tokens expire

hints: jwt.decode() never checks the signature; jwt.verify() does.
Pass { algorithms: ["HS256"] } to verify so an attacker cannot choose the algorithm.
Read process.env.JWT_SECRET once, and add { expiresIn: "15m" } when signing.
